grammar: The grammar ISO/IEC 14882 defines for `std::basic_regex` ([re.grammar]), production by production: ECMAScript's (ECMA-262, third edition, 15.10.1, the edition [intro.refs] cites, as [re.grammar] modifies it: ClassAtom and IdentityEscape modified, ClassAtomExClass, ClassAtomCollatingElement, ClassAtomEquivalence, ClassName and ClassNameCharacter added), and the regex that holds a pattern of it or of a grammar [re.synopt] selects by naming POSIX's, whose productions are POSIX BRE's and POSIX ERE's (grammars/posix-regex.json). Each production or token is mapped to the kinds of Cpp RegExp it is read into (`kinds`, each `RegExp.<tag>`, a branch of `Expressions.Cpp.RegExp.Term`), with a `note` where it is read so in some of its alternatives alone, or is listed as not a kind (`not`), with its reason: a kind's property, a container of its terms, or a union of productions mapped each on its own. Every kind of the dialect is mapped from some production; its invalid syntax, `error` and `missing`, is the framework's, which no grammar has.
checked: ISO/IEC 14882:2017, 2020 and 2024 (N4659, N4861 and N4950), whose [re.grammar] is the same in each; ECMA-262 3rd edition (1999): 32 productions and tokens, written from the standards themselves, no parser being the reference for [re.grammar]

nodes.note: [re.regex]: a regular expression, of its pattern and the syntax_option_type its flags() give, which selects its grammar ([re.synopt])

nodes.not: a regex's `flags`, the elements it is constructed with, as written: `icase`, `nosubs`, `optimize`, `collate`, `multiline` and at most one grammar element, which selects the dialect its pattern is a term of: ECMAScript's this one, `basic`, `extended`, `awk`, `grep` and `egrep` POSIX's (POSIX BRE and POSIX ERE, whose productions grammars/posix-regex.json maps)
the alternatives a pattern, a group, a capturing group or a lookahead holds, its `alternatives`
an alternative's element: an assertion, an atom, or an atom and its quantifier, a `quantifier` holding it
a quantifier's `min` and `max`, and its `raw` as written

nodes.note: `.`, `( Disjunction )`, `(?: Disjunction )`, and the third edition's lookaheads, atoms there, `(?= Disjunction )` and `(?! Disjunction )`; its other alternatives each a production of its own

nodes.not: a backslash and what it escapes, each a production of its own: a DecimalEscape, a CharacterEscape or a CharacterClassEscape
the letter of a control escape (`\cJ`), within a character's `raw`

nodes.note: as [re.grammar] modifies it: SourceCharacter but not c
`ClassAtom - ClassAtom` a range; its other alternatives a class's elements
`ClassAtomNoDash - ClassAtom` a range; its other alternatives a class's elements

nodes.not: a class's element, each of its alternatives a production of its own: `-`, a character, or [re.grammar]'s ClassAtomExClass, ClassAtomCollatingElement and ClassAtomEquivalence

nodes.note: `\b` the character backspace, `\0` NUL, a CharacterEscape a character, a CharacterClassEscape a characterset

nodes.not: an exclass's, a collating element's or an equivalence's `name`
a character of a class atom's `name`, which holds none of `.`, `=` and `:`
